title: ink — narrative scripting language, Inky editor and inklecate compiler
key_findings: ink, the Inky editor and the ink-Unity integration are free under the MIT license; the repository says attribution is not required.
Inky exports to web and to JSON, ink's compiled intermediate format; the Unity plugin recompiles ink files on edit and includes an in-editor previewer.
inkle reports that all of its games (e.g. 80 Days, Heaven's Vault, Sorcery!) were authored in ink; an Unreal integration (Inkpot) was built by The Chinese Room.
athar_applications: Candidate format for authored scene scripts and authored fallback dialogue lines, compiled to JSON and run on the web via inkjs.
Precompile per case version so the runtime never compiles author text.
limitations: Official pages checked do not mention localization or right-to-left text; Arabic editing in Inky is unverified and must be tested.
ink models branching text with variables; it has no native notion of evidence graphs or per-character knowledge scopes, so it must be bridged to the case state machine.

title: inkjs — JavaScript port of the ink engine
key_findings: MIT-licensed, zero-dependency JavaScript port that the project states is fully compatible with the original ink; runs in browsers and Node.js.
A 'full' build includes the compiler so ink source can be compiled in JavaScript; a CLI compiler (inkjs-compiler) also exists.
Compatibility table maps inkjs 2.3.0 to inklecate 1.2.0; a backward-compatible build exists for browsers without ES2015 Proxies.
athar_applications: Lets ATHAR run ink content inside a PWA and offline, with no native engine.
Same runtime can be used server-side for automated path testing.
limitations: Community-maintained (primarily two maintainers) — bus-factor risk.
Bundle size not stated; shipping the compiler to clients is unnecessary if content is precompiled.

title: Twine 2 — open-source tool for interactive nonlinear stories
key_findings: Twine publishes stories directly to HTML; simple stories need no code, while variables, conditional logic, CSS and JavaScript can be added later.
Four built-in story formats act like engines: Harlowe, SugarCube, Chapbook and Snowman.
twinery.org states that works made with Twine are free to use in any way, including commercially; the editor source on GitHub is GPL-3.0.
athar_applications: Low-cost prototyping tool for writers to sketch case branches before data entry into the ATHAR case editor.
limitations: GPL-3.0 applies to the editor: embedding or modifying the Twine editor inside a proprietary ATHAR tool would trigger copyleft obligations (legal review needed).
Passage-based model has no structured evidence/knowledge representation; RTL/Arabic UI support was not verified (GitHub locale listing could not be fetched).

title: Yarn Spinner — dialogue scripting tool for games
key_findings: Core compiler is MIT-licensed and designed to be used through engine-specific packages; the official Unity package requires Unity 2021.3+.
The project site states support for Unity, Godot (C# and GDScript) and Unreal Engine, built-in localization, and authoring in VS Code with autocomplete and live validation.
Godot C# localization exports a CSV with line IDs and context columns (original, file, node, lineNumber, lock, comment) for translators.
athar_applications: Its line-ID-per-utterance localization model is a good pattern for ATHAR's Arabic-first content with later English/French variants.
limitations: No first-party web/JavaScript runtime confirmed; engine-centric.
No mention of RTL in docs checked; VS Code authoring is unfriendly to non-programmer writers.

title: Ren'Py License
license: MIT (core) + LGPL-derived parts; bundled Zlib/BSD/Apache-2.0/MPL-2.0 components
key_findings: Ren'Py is mostly MIT-licensed, but parts derive from LGPL code, so games must be distributed in a way that satisfies the LGPL.
Bundled components carry Zlib, BSD, PNG, Apache 2.0 and MPL 2.0 licenses; the page recommends shipping license copies and linking from store descriptions.
athar_applications: Reference point only: a Python visual-novel engine is a poor fit for ATHAR's web/PWA, LLM-dialogue and evidence-graph needs.
limitations: RTL/Arabic support could not be confirmed from the translation, text or config documentation pages checked.
Not a web-first runtime.

title: Godot Engine License
key_findings: Godot is MIT (Expat) licensed: any purpose, modification and commercial redistribution, including under proprietary terms.
Game content is not covered by Godot's license; shipping the engine binary requires including its copyright notice and license text (a link in credits is described as acceptable).
Third-party components are listed in COPYRIGHT.txt with licenses described as MIT-compatible.
athar_applications: Viable no-royalty option if ATHAR later needs rich 2D/3D 'lab' mini-scenes; contrasts with Unity's pricing history.
limitations: License page is not legal advice; component licenses must still be audited.

title: Godot docs — Internationalizing games (BiDi, RTL mirroring, text server data)
key_findings: Godot automatically mirrors UI for right-to-left languages such as Arabic (anchors, margins, alignment, container child order) but not the coordinate system or non-UI nodes.
text_direction, language and layout_direction properties override defaults; a structured-text BiDi override handles paths, URLs and code.

ICU text-server data is excluded from exports by default and must be enabled (about 4 MB); TextServer can convert between Western Arabic digits and localized numerals; the default font needs replacing with a multilingual font.
athar_applications: If Godot is used for any lab scene, budget the extra ~4 MB ICU data and a proper Arabic font; test numerals and mixed Arabic/Latin forensic terms.
limitations: Docs-level claims; real Arabic shaping quality on low-end Android must be tested.

title: Godot docs — Exporting for the Web
key_findings: Godot 4 C# projects cannot currently be exported to the web; the docs point to Godot 3 for C# on web.
Web export needs WebAssembly and WebGL 2.0; multi-threaded builds need SharedArrayBuffer with COOP/COEP headers or a PWA service-worker workaround; since 4.3 single-threaded export is the default.
Web export can run on mobile with caveats (limited CPU/GPU, slower WASM); the .wasm compresses to roughly a quarter with gzip and custom templates can shrink it.
athar_applications: Do not build ATHAR's core case UI in a game engine; if a Godot mini-lab is embedded, use GDScript (not C#) and a stripped export template.
limitations: No concrete mobile-browser compatibility matrix or payload sizes given.

title: Unity is Canceling the Runtime Fee
key_findings: On 12 September 2024 Unity cancelled the Runtime Fee for games customers, effective immediately, and returned to seat-based subscriptions.
From 1 January 2025 Unity Pro rose 8% to USD 2,200 per seat per year (required above USD 200k annual revenue and funding); Enterprise rose 25% (required above USD 25M).
Unity Personal stays free with its ceiling doubled from USD 100k to 200k; the splash screen becomes optional for Unity 6 Personal games.
athar_applications: Evidence that engine terms can change materially within a year: ATHAR should keep case content engine-agnostic (own JSON schema) to avoid lock-in.
limitations: Vendor's own framing; current pricing must be re-checked at decision time.

title: Unity Runtime Fee: developers' reaction and plans to switch engines
key_findings: Reports Unity's 12 Sept 2023 announcement of a per-install Runtime Fee from 1 Jan 2024 (Personal plan: after USD 200k revenue and 200k lifetime installs, USD 0.20 per install).
Documents developer criticism (trust, retroactivity, unverifiable install counts) and some studios' stated plans to move to Godot; Godot's project manager urged against panic switching.
athar_applications: Supports a vendor-risk register entry: avoid proprietary runtimes whose pricing is tied to installs or usage the platform alone measures.
limitations: Journalism, written the day after the announcement; the fee was later cancelled (ATH-SRC-0908).

title: articy:draft X FREE
key_findings: Free version limits each project to 700 objects (flow elements, dialogue nodes/fragments, entities, assets, locations) with unlimited projects; exceeding locks the project.
Commercial rights are included in the free version and all exports are available; runs on Windows and macOS; multi-user has no free version.
athar_applications: Benchmark for what a professional narrative database offers (entities, flows, templates); ATHAR's own editor should copy the entity/template idea, not the desktop model.
limitations: Desktop, proprietary; paid prices not on the page; export formats not enumerated on the page; Arabic RTL editing unverified.

title: Arcweave pricing and plans
key_findings: Web-based narrative design platform; Basic is free (200 items per project, 3 projects, 25 AI credits/month) but cannot be used for commercial projects.

Pro is USD 15/member/month billed yearly (USD 18 monthly); Team USD 25 (30) adds project history, roles, localization, REST API and an MCP server; Enterprise adds SSO and SCORM 2004 / xAPI integrations.
JSON, CSV and engine exports (Unity, Unreal, Godot) are available on all plans.
athar_applications: Closest off-the-shelf model of a collaborative web case editor; useful for early writer prototyping, with JSON export mapped into ATHAR's schema.
limitations: SaaS lock-in and price changes; RTL not mentioned; free tier forbids commercial use.

title: Statecharts: a visual formalism for complex systems
key_findings: Foundational paper (vol. 8, issue 3, pp. 231–274) introducing statecharts as a visual formalism for complex reactive systems.
Its ideas underpin the W3C SCXML standard (which builds on Harel State Tables) and libraries such as XState that implement hierarchical, parallel and history states.
athar_applications: Model each case's progression (phases, gates, parallel investigation threads) as a statechart rather than ad-hoc flags, so it can be visualised, reviewed and exhaustively tested.
limitations: Content verified indirectly (catalog record + SCXML/XState docs); the full text was not accessible (publisher blocks fetching).
Statecharts manage control flow, not truth: they do not by themselves prevent contradictory facts.
AUDIT 2026-10-27: free to read in Elsevier open archive (OpenAlex: bronze OA; Crossref lists the Elsevier open-access user licence); still copyrighted, reuse terms not established.

title: State Chart XML (SCXML): State Machine Notation for Control Abstraction
key_findings: W3C Recommendation defining an XML, event-driven state-machine language that combines CCXML event notation with Harel State Tables.
Provides a generic execution environment for state machines, giving a vendor-neutral serialisation target.
athar_applications: A portable, standard notation if ATHAR ever needs to exchange case state machines between tools; otherwise a design reference for XState-style JSON.
limitations: Limited modern adoption outside voice/telephony; XState is inspired by but does not claim full conformance with SCXML.

title: XState — state machines and statecharts for JavaScript/TypeScript (and Stately Studio)
key_findings: MIT-licensed, dependency-free JS/TS library for state machines and statecharts with hierarchical, parallel and history states and an actor model.
Described as inspired by SCXML; v5 APIs (createMachine, createActor) run on frontend or backend.
Stately Studio is a visual editor for creating and collaborating on machines with export to XState v5.
athar_applications: Recommended runtime for the deterministic case state machine, shared by client (offline play) and server (authoritative validation).
The visual editor is a possible basis for letting writers see case flow without code.
limitations: Stately Studio is a commercial service (pricing not verified); case truth and knowledge scopes still need a separate data model.

title: XState graph utilities and model-based testing (xstate/graph)
key_findings: getShortestPaths (Dijkstra) returns one minimal path to each reachable state; getSimplePaths (DFS) returns all non-cyclic paths; getPathsFromEvents traces a given event sequence.
createTestModel turns paths into executable tests; traversal must be bounded (stopWhen/limit) when context makes the state space infinite.
Shortest paths do not cover every transition; simple paths can explode and need deduplication.
athar_applications: Automatically enumerate every route through a case (reachability of the solution, dead ends, unreachable evidence) and use those routes as seeds for simulated conversations.
limitations: Coverage is only as good as the modelled events; free-text dialogue lies outside the graph and needs separate testing.

title: Temporal — durable execution platform
key_findings: MIT-licensed durable-execution platform (a fork of Uber's Cadence) that keeps workflows running through failures by automatic retries.
Official SDKs: Go, Java, .NET, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust and TypeScript.
athar_applications: Not needed for gameplay; a candidate only for the long-running content pipeline (generate → validate → expert review → publish) once volume justifies it.
limitations: Adds a server cluster or paid cloud to operate (pricing not verified); a simple job queue is sufficient for an MVP.

title: Neo4j Licensing
key_findings: Neo4j Community Edition is listed under GPL v3; self-managed Enterprise offerings are governed by the Neo4j Software Agreement; managed cloud by the Neo4j Cloud Agreement / Aura terms.
The page says only documents referenced in an order form or click-through apply, so terms depend on the contract.
athar_applications: Avoid making a GPL/commercial graph database a hard runtime dependency for small per-case graphs; reconsider only for large cross-case analytics.
limitations: Licensing summary page, not legal advice; free-tier terms not stated on the page.

title: Memgraph Legal Policies (Community: Business Source License; Enterprise: Memgraph Enterprise License)
license: Business Source License (Community, version not stated on page); Memgraph Enterprise License
key_findings: Using Memgraph Community Edition means accepting the Business Source License; Enterprise use is under the Memgraph Enterprise License.
The page does not state a BSL version or a change date to an open-source license.
athar_applications: Source-available (not OSI open source) — treat as a licensing risk requiring legal review before any use.
limitations: BSL terms must be read in full; not verified here.

title: Apache AGE — graph extension for PostgreSQL
key_findings: Apache-2.0 PostgreSQL extension that adds graph capabilities with openCypher queries alongside SQL over one storage layer.
Supports PostgreSQL 11 through 18; release badge shows v1.8.0.
athar_applications: Lets ATHAR keep one PostgreSQL database (relational + JSONB + optional graph) for case content and cross-case analytics without a separate graph DB licence.
limitations: Availability on managed Postgres services must be checked per provider (not verified); smaller ecosystem than Neo4j.

title: Knowledge Graphs
key_findings: Broad survey (vol. 54, no. 4, pp. 1–37) comparing graph data models and query languages and the roles of schema, identity and context.
Covers deductive and inductive knowledge, and how knowledge graphs are created, enriched, quality-assessed, refined and published.
athar_applications: Grounds ATHAR's case-truth model as a small typed graph (entities, typed relations, time-qualified facts) with explicit schema and provenance per fact.
limitations: General survey; not about narrative or games; per-case graphs in ATHAR are tiny compared with the systems surveyed.

title: Narrative Planning: Balancing Plot and Character
key_findings: Introduces the IPOCL planner (vol. 39, pp. 217–268), which infers plausible character goals so each action in a generated plot is explained by character intentions.
In an empirical study, audiences understood character intentions better in IPOCL plans than in plans from conventional partial-order planners.
athar_applications: Every authored or generated action in a case timeline should carry an explicit motive link; a validator can flag 'unmotivated' actions as a fairness defect.
limitations: Planning-based generation is computationally expensive and authoring planning domains is skilled work; the study measured comprehension, not enjoyment or learning.

title: Interactive Narrative: An Intelligent Systems Approach
key_findings: Surveys about two decades of AI research on interactive narrative (vol. 34, no. 1), where users shape a dramatic storyline through choices.
Identifies what has worked and the open problems for applying computational narrative intelligence in entertainment, education and training.
athar_applications: Background map for choosing between authored branching, drama management and simulation for ATHAR's case engine.
limitations: Pre-LLM (2013); landing page did not confirm coverage of specific drama-manager techniques.

title: Structuring Content in the Façade Interactive Drama Architecture
publisher: AAAI — Proceedings of the 1st AIIDE Conference
key_findings: Façade sequences hand-authored 'beats' (27 in total, ~15 seen per playthrough) built from ~2,500 joint dialogue behaviours; a drama manager picks beats to fit a tension arc.
Player text is mapped by rules to about 30 parameterised discourse acts; the authors estimate NLU fails roughly 30% of the time in informal testing.
Authoring took about 3 person-years; the system selects pre-written content rather than generating sentences.
athar_applications: Strong precedent for 'select authored content, do not invent facts'; also a warning on authoring cost — ATHAR's LLM layer should reduce surface-text authoring, not truth authoring.
limitations: Single famous artefact; NLU failure estimate is informal; pre-LLM language understanding.

title: Versu—A Simulationist Storytelling System
publisher: IEEE Transactions on Computational Intelligence and AI in Games
key_findings: World state is a set of sentences in 'exclusion logic' (dotted paths with single-value operators), authored in the Praxis DSL with a type checker, deterministic playback and a stress-test runner.
Social practices offer role-based affordances; agents choose by simulating each candidate action, scoring the result against weighted desires, then undoing it.
Agents share one authoritative world model; false beliefs are stored as specific per-character beliefs, and nested beliefs (beliefs about beliefs) cannot be represented.
athar_applications: Model ATHAR's truth as one canonical fact store plus per-character overlays (knows / believes-false / hides); copy Versu's tooling idea of deterministic replay and mass stress tests.
limitations: Shared-world simplification makes misunderstandings hard; product (Versu) was discontinued; authoring Praxis requires programmers.

title: Sabre: A Narrative Planner Supporting Intention and Deep Theory of Mind
publisher: AAAI — Proceedings of the 17th AIIDE Conference
key_findings: Forward-chaining planner where every action must be explicable from each consenting character's believed state; beliefs can be nested to any depth.
Characters can act on false beliefs and revise them when they observe actions that contradict what they believed.
Search cost is high (largest benchmark ~6.2 hours, >105 million nodes) and, lacking uncertainty, the authors note it cannot easily handle murder mysteries.
athar_applications: Use offline only, if at all, to check that authored character actions are explicable from each character's beliefs; not a runtime component.
limitations: Computational cost; authoring fluents/actions/utilities is specialist work; DOI not confirmed in this session.

title: Answer Set Programming for Procedural Content Generation: A Design Space Approach
publisher: IEEE Transactions on Computational Intelligence and AI in Games
key_findings: Proposes describing a generator's design space declaratively in AnsProlog (vol. 3, no. 3, pp. 187–200): choice rules define possibilities, integrity constraints forbid bad artefacts, analysis rules derive properties such as solvability or solution length.
Off-the-shelf solvers (e.g. Clingo) then find artefacts satisfying all constraints, and the same model can prove properties or explain failures.
Limits: finite discrete spaces only; aesthetic qualities are hard to encode; performance unpredictable (a 21×21 maze reached a 114-step solution after about two hours).
athar_applications: Encode each case's evidence → inference rules in ASP and ask the solver: is the culprit uniquely derivable from discoverable evidence? Is every red herring refutable? Are there ≥2 minimal evidence sets?
limitations: Scaling and grounding costs; requires a specialist to write the encoding generator from the case schema.

title: clingo — answer set solver (Potassco)
key_findings: clingo combines the grounder gringo and solver clasp, with control over incremental grounding and solving; distributed under the MIT License.
Official Python packages (pip/conda) and C API; a third-party clingo-wasm project offers rudimentary in-browser use; Clingo 6 is under development (5.8 docs current).
athar_applications: Run fairness/solvability checks server-side in the publishing pipeline (Python), never on the client.
limitations: Browser builds are unofficial; solver performance depends heavily on encoding quality.

title: Procedural Puzzle Generation: A Survey
key_findings: Reviews 32 puzzle-generation methods across eleven puzzle categories (vol. 12, no. 1, pp. 21–40), compared on seven characteristics.
Notes puzzle generation has received less attention than other PCG and mostly targets dedicated puzzle games rather than puzzles embedded in narrative genres.
athar_applications: Confirms there is no mature, validated generator for narrative deduction puzzles — ATHAR should author cases and use generation only for variants and checks.
limitations: Survey up to 2019; pre-LLM.

title: Eliminating the Impossible: A Procedurally Generated Murder Mystery
publisher: CEUR Workshop Proceedings Vol-2282 (AIIDE 2018 Workshops, EXAG)
key_findings: Generates mysteries by random property assignment (unique per character) and runs the story in Ostari (dynamic epistemic logic); NPCs act on simple motives.
Solvability is argued by design: the murder leaves evidence for each culprit property, and belief tracking checks whether the player has enough evidence to accuse.
Characters never lie (listed as future work); only one small scenario (5 suspects) is shown with no quantitative evaluation.
athar_applications: Pattern: track what the player provably knows (epistemic state) and gate the accusation on it — the basis for an automated 'fair solution exists' check.
limitations: Workshop paper, tiny scope, no lies or uncertainty, no user study.

title: Murder Mystery Generation from Open Data
publisher: Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Computational Creativity (ICCC 2016)
key_findings: WikiMystery builds suspects and clues from DBpedia around a real person as victim, using a genetic algorithm whose fitness rewards solvability (each clue eliminates one innocent suspect) and diversity.
Reported limitations: template-bound dialogue/puzzles, repetitive or absurd associations from erratic open data, slow generation; only one victim tested.
athar_applications: Reusable idea: a solvability fitness = each innocent suspect must be eliminable by at least one discoverable clue.
Warning: never build teen cases around real people or uncurated open data.
limitations: Uses real individuals as victims — ethically unsuitable for ATHAR; small evaluation.

title: ClueGen: An Exploration of Procedural Storytelling in the Format of Murder Mystery Games
publisher: AAAI — Proceedings of the 12th AIIDE Conference
key_findings: Murder mystery game that generates its own storyline, using the genre's conventional structure to bound what must be generated (vol. 12, no. 2, pp. 93–99).
Main contribution: signalling deceptive characters in generated text dialogue through audio cues.
athar_applications: Design note: lies must be detectable by fair means (inconsistency with evidence), not by arbitrary tells; audio tells could be a hint-ladder aid.
limitations: Student-scale project; no robust evaluation reported on the landing page.

title: MuSR: Testing the Limits of Chain-of-thought with Multistep Soft Reasoning
key_findings: Builds ~1,000-word murder mysteries (and other narratives) with a neurosymbolic 'synthetic-to-natural' algorithm: a symbolic reasoning structure is generated first, then rendered into prose by an LLM.
Instances are solvable by human annotators with high accuracy yet challenge GPT-4 and chain-of-thought prompting.
athar_applications: Validates ATHAR's core pattern: generate/author the logical case structure first, then render language; also a ready benchmark style for testing whether an LLM 'hint helper' can be trusted to reason.
limitations: English-only; LLM scores not stated on the landing page; mysteries are text puzzles, not interactive.

title: Deciphering Digital Detectives: Understanding LLM Behaviors and Capabilities in Multi-Agent Mystery Games
key_findings: Releases a Jubensha (Chinese murder-mystery role-play) dataset with character scripts and rules, and a framework where LLM agents play without humans.
Proposes metrics for agents' retention of case details and reasoning, and in-context methods to improve information gathering and culprit identification.
athar_applications: Shows the market/research interest in LLM-driven murder-mystery role-play (adjacent to ATHAR); useful source of metric ideas for character fact retention.
limitations: Preprint; peer-review status not confirmed; no quantitative results in the abstract.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
key_findings: Agents store a natural-language memory stream, synthesise reflections, and retrieve memories to plan; ablation shows observation, planning and reflection each matter for believability (25-agent sandbox town).

Reported failures include missed memory retrieval, embellishment (agents adding events that never happened or attributing knowledge from the base model), and overly polite/agreeable behaviour from instruction tuning.
Running 25 agents for two game days cost 'thousands of dollars' in tokens, per the authors.
athar_applications: Do not use free-form memory streams as case truth: embellishment is exactly the 'invented evidence' failure ATHAR must prevent. Borrow retrieval + reflection only for non-evidential colour.
limitations: Evaluation over a short timescale against crowdworker baselines; costs reflect 2023 model prices.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
publisher: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS 2020)
key_findings: Combines a seq2seq generator (parametric memory) with a dense retriever over a Wikipedia index (non-parametric memory); pp. 9459–9474.
Set state of the art on three open-domain QA tasks and produced more specific, diverse and factual generations than a parametric-only baseline.
athar_applications: Retrieval should be scoped per character: the 'index' a character may draw on is its knowledge scope, not the whole case; for a small case, deterministic lookup beats vector search.
limitations: Retrieval reduces but does not eliminate unsupported generation; designed for open-domain QA, not role-play with secrets.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
publisher: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
key_findings: Performance on multi-document QA and key-value retrieval is highest when relevant information is at the start or end of the context and drops when it is in the middle (vol. 12, pp. 157–173).
Holds even for models built for long contexts.
athar_applications: Keep each character prompt short and ordered: rules and allowed facts at the top, the player's question at the end; never paste the whole case file.
limitations: Measured on 2023 models; newer models may degrade less, so re-test with ATHAR's chosen model.

title: Claude API docs — Structured outputs
key_findings: Constrained decoding makes responses follow a supplied JSON schema (output_config.format) and strict tool use validates tool inputs; schema violations need no retries.
Unsupported schema features include recursive schemas, numeric and string-length constraints, and additionalProperties other than false; complexity limits apply and grammars are cached for 24 hours.
Refusals and max_tokens truncation can still yield non-conforming output; the guarantee is structural, not factual.
athar_applications: Force every character turn into a small schema (utterance_ar + cited fact_ids + reveal flags) so a deterministic validator can check knowledge boundaries.
limitations: Vendor doc; feature list changes; schema compliance says nothing about truthfulness.

title: OpenAI API docs — Structured Outputs
key_findings: Structured Outputs (strict: true) ensures responses adhere to a supplied JSON Schema so required keys are not omitted and enum values are not invented; older JSON mode guarantees only valid JSON.
Available via function calling or a json_schema response format; safety refusals are programmatically detectable.
athar_applications: Confirms the pattern is multi-vendor, so ATHAR's dialogue contract can stay vendor-neutral.
limitations: The fetched page did not list the supported schema subset; vendor doc.

title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models
key_findings: Format-restricted generation (e.g. JSON) noticeably reduced LLM reasoning performance compared with free-form answers (pp. 1218–1236).
Stricter format constraints generally caused larger drops on reasoning tasks.
athar_applications: For the assessment judge, let the model reason in free text first and emit the structured verdict last (or in a second call); keep dialogue schemas minimal.
limitations: Tested models/tasks of 2024; newer constrained-decoding implementations may differ.

title: Claude docs — Reduce hallucinations
key_findings: Recommends allowing 'I don't know', grounding on extracted direct quotes, requiring a supporting quote for each claim (and retracting unsupported claims), and restricting answers to provided documents.
Advanced: best-of-N comparison to expose inconsistencies, iterative self-verification; the page states these reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations.
athar_applications: Encode 'I don't know / I didn't see that' as a first-class, scored behaviour for characters; require each factual claim to cite a fact_id.
limitations: Vendor guidance without published effect sizes.

title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
key_findings: Samples several responses; facts that recur are likely grounded while divergent/contradictory ones are likely hallucinated (pp. 9004–9017).
Works black-box with no external database and outperformed grey-box baselines on WikiBio passages.
athar_applications: Secondary offline detector in test suites; for ATHAR, checking against the canonical fact store is stronger and cheaper than self-consistency.
limitations: Consistent hallucinations are not detected; multiplies inference cost; evaluated in English biography domain.
AUDIT 2026-10-27: licence confirmed as CC BY 4.0 via the ACL Anthology page licence (CC BY 4.0); rights corrected from UNKNOWN (attribution required).

title: SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization
publisher: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
key_findings: NLI models detect summary inconsistency well when applied at sentence granularity and aggregated (SummaCConv), reaching 74.4% balanced accuracy on a six-dataset benchmark (vol. 10, pp. 163–177).
Attributes earlier NLI failures to a granularity mismatch between sentence-level NLI and document-level checking.
athar_applications: Check each generated character sentence against the allowed fact statements (sentence-level), flagging contradiction or unsupported content.
limitations: ~74% balanced accuracy means many errors: use as triage with human review, not as a gate alone; English models — Arabic NLI quality must be validated.

title: TimeChara: Evaluating Point-in-Time Character Hallucination of Role-Playing Large Language Models
publisher: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
key_findings: Defines 'point-in-time character hallucination': a role-playing model reveals knowledge inconsistent with the character's identity or position in the story timeline (pp. 3291–3325).
A 10,895-instance benchmark found significant hallucination even in state-of-the-art models including GPT-4o.
The proposed Narrative-Experts decomposition reduces such errors, but the authors state the problem remains open.
athar_applications: Directly supports enforcing knowledge scopes outside the model (data filtering) rather than relying on prompts like 'pretend you don't know X'.
limitations: Built on well-known fictional franchises (where the base model knows the plot); ATHAR's original cases may behave differently — must be tested.

title: Character-LLM: A Trainable Agent for Role-Playing
publisher: Proceedings of EMNLP 2023 (Association for Computational Linguistics), pp. 13153-13187
key_findings: Trains LLMs to portray specific historical figures by converting character profiles into 'experiences' used as training data, rather than prompting alone.
Evaluates agents by interviewing them to test retention of the character's background.

Adds 'protective experiences': training scenes in which the character is pressed on out-of-era knowledge and responds with ignorance; authors report agents generalise to new provoking questions, mitigating 'character hallucination'.
athar_applications: Fine-tuning per character is too costly for ATHAR's case volume; prefer data-level scoping at inference time.
limitations: Venue confirmed (EMNLP 2023 main, Singapore) and mechanism read in the PDF on 2026-10-27 (gap-fill); evaluation relies partly on LLM judges; English historical figures; mitigation, not elimination.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
key_findings: Strong judges such as GPT-4 reached over 80% agreement with human preferences, about the level of agreement between humans.
Identifies position bias, verbosity bias and self-enhancement bias, and limited reasoning when grading; proposes partial mitigations.
athar_applications: LLM judging of learner justifications is feasible only with ATHAR-specific calibration against Arabic human raters and bias controls (position swap, length control, reference answers).
limitations: Measures preference agreement on chat answers, not validity of educational scoring; English; GPT-4-era.

title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
key_findings: Swapping the order of candidate responses can change LLM-judge rankings; e.g. Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT on 66 of 80 queries when ChatGPT was the judge (pp. 9440–9450).
A calibration framework reduced the bias and aligned judgments more closely with human annotations.
athar_applications: Never compare two learner answers in a single judge prompt without order swapping; prefer absolute rubric scoring against a reference.
limitations: Pairwise setting; specific calibration method names not confirmed from the landing page.

title: Verbosity Bias in Preference Labeling by Large Language Models
key_findings: GPT-4 preferred longer answers more strongly than human raters did when quality was similar; proposes a metric for verbosity bias.
athar_applications: Teens' short but correct justifications must not be penalised: include length-controlled anchors and short exemplar answers in rubrics.
limitations: Preprint; peer-review status not confirmed.

title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
key_findings: GPT-4 and Llama 2 can distinguish their own outputs better than chance; fine-tuning experiments show a linear link between self-recognition and self-preference, suggested to be causal.
athar_applications: Use a different model (or family) to judge than the one generating hints/model answers; avoid judging AI-polished learner text against AI-written references.
limitations: Preprint; peer-review status not confirmed in this session.

title: Justice or Prejudice? Quantifying Biases in LLM-as-a-Judge
key_findings: Identifies 12 potential biases in LLM-as-a-judge and the CALM framework that quantifies each by systematically perturbing evaluation inputs.
Advanced models perform well overall but significant biases persist on specific tasks.
athar_applications: Template for an ATHAR judge 'bias audit' before each model change: perturb order, length, authority cues and style, measure score shifts.
limitations: Preprint; peer-review status not confirmed in this session.

title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
key_findings: Chain-of-thought plus a form-filling evaluation protocol reached a Spearman correlation of 0.514 with human judgments on summarization (pp. 2511–2522).
Flags a preliminary bias of LLM evaluators toward LLM-generated text.
athar_applications: Even 'state of the art' correlations are moderate: use LLM scores as one signal with human moderation, not as sole grade.
limitations: Summarization/dialogue NLG, not reasoning assessment.
AUDIT 2026-10-27: licence confirmed as CC BY 4.0 via the ACL Anthology page licence (CC BY 4.0); rights corrected from UNKNOWN (attribution required).

title: Prometheus: Inducing Fine-grained Evaluation Capability in Language Models
key_findings: An open 13B evaluator trained on 1K rubrics/100K feedback examples reached Pearson 0.897 with human evaluators on 45 customised rubrics, close to GPT-4 (0.882).
Requires a score rubric and benefits from a reference answer.
athar_applications: Supports rubric-plus-reference judging and the option of a small self-hosted judge model to cut cost and keep learner text in-house.
limitations: Preprint version checked (venue not confirmed); English; rubrics authored for the benchmark, not for education.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
key_findings: 2025 edition (latest listed) ranks: LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM03 Supply Chain, LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning, LLM05 Improper Output Handling.
Continues: LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses, LLM09 Misinformation, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption.
athar_applications: Threat model for ATHAR characters: assume the system prompt will leak (so never put the case solution in it), treat player text as untrusted, cap usage per user/session.
limitations: Community list; not a certification; no teen-specific guidance.

title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
publisher: ACM — Proceedings of the 16th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec 2023)
key_findings: LLM-integrated applications blur data and instructions, so prompts planted in retrieved content can remotely steer the application (pp. 79–90).
Demonstrated against real systems (e.g. Bing Chat) and reported that effective mitigations were lacking.
athar_applications: Any user-generated content (community cases, player notes, uploaded text) that a character might read is an injection channel; keep it out of character prompts or sanitise and fence it.
limitations: 2023 systems; defences have evolved but the class of attack remains (OWASP LLM01).

title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
key_findings: Argues injections succeed because models treat system prompts and untrusted text with equal priority; trains GPT-3.5 to ignore lower-privileged conflicting instructions.
Reports large robustness gains, including on unseen attack types, with minimal capability loss (no figures on the abstract page).
athar_applications: Prefer models trained with an instruction hierarchy, but never rely on it alone: architecture (no secrets in prompt) is the primary control.
limitations: Company preprint; vendor-specific; effect sizes not on landing page.

title: Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
key_findings: Llama2-7B-based classifier that labels both user prompts and model responses against a customisable safety taxonomy; matches or beats moderation tools on OpenAI Moderation and ToxicChat benchmarks.
Instruction-tuned so categories and output format can be adapted; weights released.
athar_applications: Pattern for a separate input/output safety classifier with an ATHAR teen-specific taxonomy (self-harm, sexual content, real-crime glorification, personal data), run before and after the character model.
limitations: English-centric benchmarks; Arabic and dialect performance must be measured; superseded versions exist (not reviewed here).

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
key_findings: Companion profile to the AI RMF 1.0 (published 26 July 2024) listing 12 GAI risks, including confabulation, data privacy, harmful bias/homogenisation, human-AI configuration, information integrity, information security and intellectual property.
Defines confabulation as confidently presented false or fabricated content, sometimes contradicting the prompt or the system's own earlier statements.
athar_applications: Use the 12-risk list as the skeleton of ATHAR's AI risk register and governance review.
limitations: US voluntary framework; not specific to children or games. Likely a US federal work, but reuse status was not confirmed on the page.

title: Testing ChoiceScript Games Automatically (Quicktest and Randomtest)
key_findings: Quicktest systematically tries every option and both sides of every condition, reporting errors and untested (likely dead) lines, with some false positives.

Randomtest plays the game many times (10,000+ recommended) with a fixed seed for reproducibility, logs choices and reports per-line hit counts; an 'avoid used options' mode speeds coverage but can miss bugs.
The two tools find different bugs and neither replaces manual testing.
athar_applications: Direct template for ATHAR's case CI: exhaustive structural pass + seeded random/persona playthroughs with coverage heatmaps per evidence node and dialogue topic.
limitations: Built for deterministic branching text; LLM dialogue adds non-determinism that needs semantic checks.

title: IEEE 9274.1.1-2023 — IEEE Standard for Learning Technology: JSON Data Model Format and RESTful Web Service for Learner Experience Data Tracking and Access (xAPI)
key_findings: Active IEEE standard (board approval 30 March 2023, published 6 October 2023) standardising xAPI's JSON data model and RESTful service; a related ISO/IEC/IEEE 39274-1-1-2025 is listed.
xAPI records actor-verb-object statements sent to a Learning Record Store (LRS) that can share data with other LRSs (per xapi.com overview).
athar_applications: Only for institutional deployments: map ATHAR's internal events to xAPI statements at an export boundary, with pseudonymous actor accounts.
limitations: Standard text is paid; xAPI's cross-organisation data sharing raises privacy questions not addressed in the overview page.

title: 1EdTech Learning Tools Interoperability (LTI) 1.3 and LTI Advantage
key_findings: LTI connects external tools to an institution's learning platform without separate logins; LTI 1.3 uses the 1EdTech Security Framework (OAuth2 + JSON Web Tokens).
LTI Advantage services: Names and Role Provisioning, Assignment and Grade Services (grade passback) and Deep Linking; certification via a conformance suite and TrustEd Apps directory.
athar_applications: Phase-2 school pilots: launch a case from a school LMS and post a rubric score back via AGS, sending only the minimum identifiers.
limitations: Certification needs membership/login; not needed for the consumer app.

title: 1EdTech Caliper Analytics 1.2
key_findings: Standard vocabulary and metric profiles (16, e.g. Assessment, Session, Tool Use, Feedback) for collecting learning-activity data from digital resources.
Described as collecting click-stream data from all digital resources; certification and sensor APIs are member-only.
athar_applications: Only if a ministry/LMS partner mandates it; ATHAR should keep its own minimal event model and export to Caliper or xAPI on demand.
limitations: Page gives no Caliper-specific privacy guidance; click-stream scope conflicts with data minimisation for minors.

title: NIST SP 800-226: Guidelines for Evaluating Differential Privacy Guarantees
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
key_findings: Final guidance (March 2025) explaining differential privacy as a way to quantify privacy loss from including a person's data in a dataset.
Introduces a 'differential privacy pyramid' of factors and catalogues common implementation pitfalls ('privacy hazards').
athar_applications: Use when ATHAR publishes aggregate learning statistics (e.g. to schools or in research) to bound re-identification risk of minors.
limitations: Technical guidance; DP adds noise that harms small-cohort (single-class) reports.

title: RAPPOR: Randomized Aggregatable Privacy-Preserving Ordinal Response
key_findings: Collects population statistics from client software using randomized response so that individual reports are unlinkable and cannot be inspected individually (pp. 1054–1067).
Provides differential-privacy and utility guarantees and was evaluated on synthetic and real data.
athar_applications: Pattern for product telemetry that does not need per-learner records (e.g. which hint level is most used), randomised on device before upload.
limitations: Needs large populations for accurate estimates; not suitable for individual learner feedback.

title: The Offline Cookbook
key_findings: Catalogues when to cache (on install as dependency or not, on activate, on user interaction, on network response, stale-while-revalidate, push, background sync).
Catalogues how to serve (cache-only, network-only, cache-first, network-first, cache-then-network, race, generic fallback); patterns are combined per URL.
athar_applications: Case pack (truth-free client bundle, authored lines, images) cached on explicit 'download case for offline'; telemetry queued and synced in background.
limitations: Page shows an old 'last updated' date (2014-12-09); APIs evolved since; browser support differs (notably iOS).

title: MDN — Storage quotas and eviction criteria
key_findings: Best-effort storage can be evicted under pressure (LRU by origin); persistent storage via navigator.storage.persist() is evicted only by the user.

Safari (with tracking prevention) proactively deletes script-written data for origins without user interaction in the last seven days of browser use; home-screen apps share the browser quota and the page does not say they are exempt.
athar_applications: Never store the only copy of progress on the device: sync to server when online; request persistent storage; design for re-download of case packs.
limitations: Browser policies change; quotas vary per device.

title: Claude API docs — Prompt caching
key_findings: Caches an exact prompt prefix (tools → system → messages); default 5-minute TTL refreshed on use, optional 1-hour TTL.
Pricing relative to base input: 5-min cache write 1.25×, 1-hour write 2×, cache read 0.1× (0.05× on some current models).
Any byte change in the prefix (timestamps, unstable JSON key order, tool changes) causes a miss; minimum cacheable length varies by model (e.g. 512–4,096 tokens).
athar_applications: Order character prompts as: stable safety rules + character card + case-scoped facts (cached) → current state delta → player turn; serialise JSON deterministically.
limitations: Vendor pricing changes; per-character prefixes may fall below minimum length.

title: OpenAI API docs — Prompt caching
key_findings: Caching is automatic on supported models; for newer models the prefix must be ≥1,024 tokens, cache reads cost 0.1× input (or less on some models) and writes 1.25× (2.5× for 12-hour retention).
Best practice: static content first, append rather than rewrite turns, keep tools stable, prewarm shared context, monitor hit rates.
athar_applications: Confirms caching economics are cross-vendor; ATHAR's prompt layout can be vendor-neutral.
limitations: Vendor-specific numbers that change frequently.

title: Claude API docs — Batch processing (Message Batches API)
key_findings: Batch requests are billed at 50% of standard prices; up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch; most finish within an hour and unfinished ones expire after 24 hours.
Batch and prompt-caching discounts stack, with best-effort cache hit rates (typically 30%–98%).
athar_applications: Precompute offline: authored-line variants, test-conversation suites, judge calibration runs and nightly regression audits at half price.
limitations: Not usable for real-time dialogue.

title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
key_findings: Groups cost strategies into prompt adaptation, LLM approximation (e.g. caching, smaller models) and LLM cascades.
A learned cascade matched the best single model with up to 98% cost reduction, or improved accuracy ~4% at equal cost, on the authors' tasks.
athar_applications: Route most character turns to a small model; escalate to a large model only when the validator rejects or the turn is a high-stakes confrontation.
limitations: 'Up to 98%' is a best case on specific 2023 tasks; preprint version checked.

title: Language Model Tokenizers Introduce Unfairness Between Languages
key_findings: The same content can need up to 15× more tokens in some languages than in English, raising cost and latency and reducing usable context.
Reports that the cl100k_base tokenizer (ChatGPT/GPT-4) uses about 3× more tokens for Arabic than English; multilingual tokenizers such as XLM-R (1.18) or BLOOM (1.14) show much smaller premiums.
athar_applications: Arabic-first dialogue may cost a multiple of English per turn: benchmark token counts per candidate model with real ATHAR Arabic text before choosing a vendor.
limitations: Tokenizers measured in 2023; newer vendor tokenizers may differ — must be re-measured.

title: Ren'Py documentation: Changelog (Arabic text shaping; RTL enabled by default) and reading_order style property
key_findings: 8.3.7: with config.rtl and the HarfBuzz shaper (Ren'Py 8 only), Ren'Py unmaps Arabic presentation forms and lets HarfBuzz fully shape Arabic, so fonts without presentation forms work.
8.4.1 / 8.5.0 changelog entries: support for right-to-left languages is now enabled by default (config.rtl no longer needs to be set).
A reading_order style property (ltr, rtl, wltr, wrtl) controls directionally neutral lines; a bidi regression in mixed LTR/RTL runs was fixed.
athar_applications: Ren'Py is no longer 'RTL unverified': it is a credible Arabic prototyping option, though still desktop-first and not web-first for ATHAR's PWA.
limitations: Documentation claims, not tested by us with Arabic diacritics, digits or mixed Latin identifiers.

title: Twine 2 source: supported UI locales list (src/util/locales.ts)
key_findings: The Twine 2 editor's supported UI locales (22 entries) include no Arabic or other RTL language.
athar_applications: Arab writers would use Twine's editor UI in a non-Arabic language; story text direction then depends on story format CSS (not verified). Reinforces building ATHAR's own RTL-native editor.
limitations: Reflects the develop branch at fetch time; RTL behaviour of story formats (Harlowe, SugarCube) not mentioned in their docs fetched this round.

title: Writing with ink - Part 6: International character support in identifiers
key_findings: ink places no limits on non-ASCII characters in story content.
Identifiers (variables, knots, stitches, diverts) may use a predefined set of non-ASCII ranges, including a subset of the Arabic block U+0600-U+06FF.
athar_applications: Arabic text and Arabic identifiers are supported at the language level; RTL editing in the Inky editor and RTL display remain the runtime/UI's job (untested).
limitations: Says nothing about bidirectional display or Inky editor RTL behaviour.

title: Arcweave documentation: Localization
key_findings: Localization is available only in Team workspaces; the main language can be changed from English; other languages are edited in a Translation Mode that blocks adding or deleting items.
Arcscript segments can be marked translatable; the docs include an Arabic rendering example.
No statement found on right-to-left editor UI.
athar_applications: Arcweave can hold Arabic content and translations, but Arabic-first authoring needs Arabic as main language on a paid Team plan; RTL editor usability must be tested with writers.
limitations: Docs page only; behaviour of RTL in the canvas editor not verified.

title: Measuring digital development: Facts and Figures 2025 (Internet use; Mobile network coverage)
key_findings: Internet use in the Arab States region is about 70% of the population (Asia-Pacific 77%), roughly in line with the global average; Africa 36%.
5G population coverage in the Arab States region is about 13% (Europe 74%), while 4G remains the main reliable connectivity layer.
Globally about 2.2 billion people remain offline.
athar_applications: Size bundles and media for 4G and intermittent connectivity, not 5G; offline-first PWA remains justified for the region as a whole.
limitations: Regional averages hide very large country gaps (GCC vs low-income states); figures are ITU estimates.

title: The Mobile Economy Middle East and North Africa 2025
key_findings: 308 million mobile internet users in MENA in 2024 (46% of population), projected 378 million (52%) by 2030; about 340 million covered but not using mobile internet (usage gap).
Mobile internet penetration 71% in GCC vs 43% in low- and middle-income MENA countries; 4G was 65% of connections and 5G 7% in 2024 (5G projected 48% by 2030).
30% of users still rely on 3G or feature phones; an entry-level smartphone costs a median 18% of monthly GDP per capita (44% for the poorest 20%).
athar_applications: Plan for low-end Android, 3G/4G fallback and small downloads outside the GCC; treat a GCC-first launch as a different device/bandwidth profile from Levant/North Africa.
limitations: Industry-association figures; MENA definition differs from ITU 'Arab States'; summary PDF only.
